newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PRESIDENT REFUSES TO SIGN SECURITIES BILL.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PRESIDENT REFUSES TO SIGN SECURITIES BILL.

text.p: Slovak President Michal Kovac has refused to sign a controversial amendment to the securities law and returned it to parliament for revision, his office said in a statement on Wednesday.

"The President has asked deputies to alter the law to explicitly stipulate that a majority shareholder cannot suspend trading of its issue on the stock market," the statement said adding he also asked parliament to omit a clause allowing trading with shares outside organised markets.
The new securities legislation, approved by parliament earlier this month, effectively reinstated securities trading outside organised markets.
The new measure also reversed the previous law according to which all transactions had to be registered on the Central Securities Registry and performed through brokers on organised markets.

Analysts said they feared that allowing trading with shares outside the scrutiny of the market would severly damage already poor market transparency, as it could lead to sales to completely unknown buyers.

"The obligation to register shares and trades with them in the official register had a positive influence on organisation of the Slovak capital market and withdrawing this rules would be a step back," the President's statement said.

Though parliament rejected the most controversial proposal in the amendment explicitly giving majority shareholders the right to suspend trading in an issue, the amended law dropped a stipulation expressly forbidding such a move from the previous legislation.
"If something is not forbidden by law, then it is allowed," Dusan Lachkovic, President of the Slovak Association of Investment Companies, said shortly after the parliamentary vote.
